purpose: Rejected experiment: vectorize PgfWaveletTransform.InverseRow (horizontal wavelet lifting), the one lifting pass the earlier pgf-codec-allocation-and-simd.md PRD left scalar (only the vertical/column pass was vectorized there). The lifting recurrence separates into two independent passes (all even positions using original odd neighbors, then all odd positions using the now-final even neighbors), so each pass's writes are mutually independent - implemented as gather-into-scratch-buffer, Vector<int> arithmetic, scatter-back, per pass, with an unchanged scalar fallback (renamed InverseRowScalar) for ForceScalarVectorsForTesting and non-accelerated runtimes. before-*/after-* are a controlled MediumRun (N>=15) of the two decode-shaped SessionWorkloadBenchmarks (DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession, ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession, both ForceScalarVectors values), same machine/job/fixtures as the workspace-decode-buffer experiment's before run (docs/benchmarks/pgfcodec/2026-08-06-445451b-workspace-decode-buffer-rejected/before-*), since PgfWaveletTransform.cs was untouched between that baseline and this experiment.
sourceArtifactDirectories: docs/benchmarks/pgfcodec/2026-08-06-445451b-workspace-decode-buffer-rejected (before, reused - PgfWaveletTransform.cs was unchanged between that baseline and this experiment)
result: REJECTED, decisively. Full codec suite (1397/1397, including 4 new focused parity tests comparing the vectorized path against ForceScalarVectorsForTesting=true across widths chosen to stress every vector-width remainder case) and the Browser/WASM build were green - this was a correct, byte-exact implementation, not a bug. But MediumRun timing (AMD Ryzen 7 5800X) shows a clear regression, not a wash: DecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False, vectorized row lifting enabled) 121.7ms -> 143.7ms (+18.1%); ProgressiveDecodeFiftyImagesInNewSession(False) 133.7ms -> 156.0ms (+16.7%). ForceScalarVectors=True (forced scalar - InverseRowScalar is byte-for-byte the original single-pass code) stayed flat versus baseline (138.4ms -> 138.7ms; 153.3ms -> 150.2ms, both within noise), confirming the regression is specifically the two-pass vectorized replacement, not some unrelated change. Root cause, matching the pre-implementation risk assessment: splitting one cache-friendly fused interleaved pass into two separate full passes over the row (even pass, then odd pass) doubles how many times each row's memory is touched, and the per-chunk gather-into-scratch-buffer/scatter-back required because even/odd operands are stride-2 (not contiguous, so plain Vector<int> loads cannot read them directly) adds real overhead on top of that - together these costs substantially exceed the small (~4 ops/element) arithmetic this filter ever had to save. Reverted; PgfWaveletTransform.cs and PgfWaveletTransformTests.cs changes were not committed. Do not retry this specific two-pass-plus-gather approach without a fundamentally different, cheaper way to get even/odd operands into vector lanes (e.g. real deinterleave/shuffle intrinsics, which would abandon this codebase's portable Vector<T> convention and need a separate WASM/ARM-safe fallback story) or a demonstrated reason the gather/scatter and double-pass costs would be smaller on some other workload shape than the one measured here.
